YR5WdGrpoug.summary: Rich Hickey's Clojure/Conj 2018 keynote argues that Maybe/Option types and rigid type signatures are a poor way to model data that changes over time. He builds the case around optionality, schema growth and compatibility, and presents the ideas behind Clojure spec as an alternative.
YR5WdGrpoug.why: HN commenters send people to it whenever nulls, Maybe/Option or static typing come up, as a thoughtful dissent from the type-system orthodoxy that changes how some people model data.

YSfCdBBqNXY.summary: Dr. Russell Barkley gives a nearly three-hour lecture of essential ideas about ADHD for parents, covering what ADHD is, its effects on executive function, motivation and emotion, and how it affects children.
YSfCdBBqNXY.why: HN readers recommend it as the best primer for understanding ADHD at a neurological level, often suggesting that even the first 10 to 20 minutes are enlightening.

YEBfamv-_do.summary: A short explainer on the history and mechanics of public key cryptography and the Diffie-Hellman key exchange. It uses a mixing-paint-colors analogy to show how two parties can agree on a shared secret in public.
YEBfamv-_do.why: It is the go-to beginner explanation of Diffie-Hellman, recommended because the paint analogy makes the idea click without prior cryptography knowledge.

YnWhqhNdYyk.summary: Kate Gregory argues at CppCon 2015 that C++ should be taught without starting from C: no char* strings, printf or raw arrays at first, with references before pointers.
YnWhqhNdYyk.why: HN people cite it constantly in C versus C++ debates as the case for teaching modern C++ idioms rather than C first.

YQ_xWvX1n9g.summary: Dan Olson's roughly two-hour video essay critiques NFTs, cryptocurrency, and Web3, covering their technical, economic, and ideological flaws. It is heavily sourced and ends with the advice to ask whether a project needs crypto to work.
YQ_xWvX1n9g.why: It is the go-to long-form critique of crypto that HN commenters recommend whenever skeptics ask for a thorough, well-researched takedown.

YKuRkGkf5HU.summary: Emily Shea explains how repetitive strain injury pushed her to program by voice using speech recognition (Talon), and gives a live coding demo. She argues voice-driven development can be pain-free, efficient and enjoyable.
YKuRkGkf5HU.why: It is the go-to recommendation whenever someone asks about voice coding or RSI-friendly programming setups.

Y9FZ4igNxNA.summary: Huygens Optics explains the Fourier transform and shows how a lens performs one optically. A DLP projector is used as a Fourier filter to do simple pattern recognition on lithographic character patterns.
Y9FZ4igNxNA.why: Recommended as one of the best explanations of Fourier transforms and a clear demo of analog optical computing.

YThelfB2fvg.summary: Posy gives a short history of the computer mouse cursor, from early straight pointers to the tilted arrow, comparing Apple and Windows designs. He then explains why he designed his own cursor set and offers it as a free download.
YThelfB2fvg.why: HN treats it as the definitive, short, well-made video on mouse cursors and pulls it out whenever cursor design, pixel perfection or the tilted arrow comes up.

YX3iRjKj7C0.summary: Robert Martin's RailsConf 2009 talk looks at why Smalltalk lost out despite its technical strengths. He draws lessons about language communities and arrogance that he argues could hurt Ruby too.
YX3iRjKj7C0.why: HN cites it in discussions of language evangelism, community dynamics and zealotry, as an accessible account of how a good language can die for non-technical reasons.

YX40hbAHx3s.summary: An 11-minute animated introduction to P vs. NP and the wider landscape of complexity classes, inspired by the Complexity Zoo wiki. It assumes no background in computer science.
YX40hbAHx3s.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best short, funny introduction to P vs. NP and complexity classes for people with no background.

Yocja_N5s1I.summary: The first episode of Crash Course World History, in which John Green covers the shift from hunting and gathering to agriculture and how it shaped civilization. It is delivered fast and with jokes.
Yocja_N5s1I.why: HN recommends the series as a funny, coherent high-school-level overview of world history that teaches a lot in a few hours.

Y6U728AZnV0.summary: Cardiologist James O'Keefe argues in a TEDx talk that moderate running confers the best longevity benefits, while extreme endurance training can damage the heart. He draws on data and his own experience as a lifelong runner.
Y6U728AZnV0.why: HN cites it whenever people question whether more exercise is always better, especially extreme endurance running.

YyIQKBzIuBY.summary: An Alan Kay talk on programming and scaling, covering theoretical limits of code size, engineering versus tinkering, and biological cells as inspiration for object-oriented design.
YyIQKBzIuBY.why: HN fans call it one of Kay's best talks and recommend it for rethinking why programming paradigms have barely changed.

Y3n3c_8Nn2Y.summary: A recording of .the .product by Farbrausch, the first-place 64k intro at The Party 2000. It fits an 11-minute 3D demo with music into 64 kilobytes.
Y3n3c_8Nn2Y.why: HN commenters use it as the standard example of how much a tiny program can do, in contrast to bloated modern software.

Y5K9HBiJpuk.summary: Mentour Pilot's 56-minute account of the MH370 disappearance and what is now known, including the WSPR radio tracking technique and other sensing methods. It was made ahead of renewed search efforts.
Y5K9HBiJpuk.why: HN recommends it as a detailed, pilot's-eye summary of the whole MH370 story and the case for searching again.

YpuX-5E7xoU.summary: FortNine looks at the data on why newer pickup trucks with tall, blunt grilles kill so many pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists. It argues that lowering hood height would substantially cut fatalities.
YpuX-5E7xoU.why: HN people cite it in threads on vehicle size and safety as a clear explanation tying grille height to deaths.

YSLV7t9DvN8.summary: The six Norton Lectures Jorge Luis Borges gave in 1967-68, titled This Craft of Verse, on topics including the riddle of poetry, metaphor, storytelling, translation and a poet's creed. The recording runs over four hours.
YSLV7t9DvN8.why: Strongly recommended as under-appreciated lectures showing Borges' erudition, delivered in a hypnotic voice from memory.

YbZ3zDzDnrw.summary: John Ousterhout lectures on the Raft consensus algorithm, made for the Raft user study comparing how students learn Raft and Paxos. It covers leader election and log repair.
YbZ3zDzDnrw.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clearer introduction to Raft than the paper and as part of a well-designed understandability study.

Y0Oa4Lp5fLE.summary: Stanford biologist Robert Sapolsky lectures on the evolution of behavior, including the Prisoner's Dilemma and tit-for-tat strategies in animals. It is part of his Human Behavioral Biology course.
Y0Oa4Lp5fLE.why: Recommended in game-theory and cooperation threads, with the whole lecture series endorsed.

Y99Wj-NStok.summary: Summoning Salt traces the speedrunning history of Mario Kart 64's Choco Mountain track and its famous shortcut, through the successive record holders and discoveries. It carries an epilepsy warning for flickering lights.
Y99Wj-NStok.why: HN recommends it as a gripping entry point into speedrunning and as a model of a well-made history video.

YCjNT9qGjh4.summary: Valve's two-hour documentary for Half-Life 2's 20th anniversary, with team members discussing development, nearly running out of money, being hacked, the publisher lawsuit and the birth of Steam.
YCjNT9qGjh4.why: HN recommends it as an excellent inside look at Valve's history, its technology and the games industry of the time.

YI3tsmFsrOg.summary: An animated Kurzgesagt explainer on bacteriophages, viruses that kill bacteria, covering how they infect and burst cells and their potential as therapy against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
YI3tsmFsrOg.why: HN commenters link it whenever phage therapy or antibiotic resistance comes up, as an accessible overview.

YuIIjLr6vUA.summary: Mathologer examines the infamous Numberphile claim that 1+2+3+... equals -1/12, explaining what is wrong with the calculation and how it connects to real math like the zeta function and analytic continuation.
YuIIjLr6vUA.why: HN points to it as the in-depth rebuttal to the Numberphile video that explains why the 'proof' is wrong yet the result is meaningful.

Y4Gt3Xjd7G8.summary: David Beazley's workshop screencast builds asynchronous programming in Python from scratch, starting from callbacks and continuations and replacing threads to show how concurrency works underneath.
Y4Gt3Xjd7G8.why: HN people recommend it as the best way to understand what async machinery actually does under the covers.

YpllomiDMX0.summary: Dr. Jason Fung lectures on why obesity became an epidemic since the 1970s, arguing insulin and hormones rather than calories drive weight gain. He explains why calorie counting fails and touches on low-carb eating and fasting.
YpllomiDMX0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a compelling alternative explanation of obesity from a prominent proponent.

YycAzdtUIko.summary: A PBS Space Time episode hosted by Gabe Perez-Giz on the nature of spacetime and whether space and time are fundamental. It builds up reference frames and causality in a short, dense format.
YycAzdtUIko.why: HN commenters point to the PBS Space Time series as a high-quality, bite-sized way to learn modern physics concepts.

Y65FRxE7uMc.summary: Tom 7's pilot episode of a series that plays with type systems and absurd programming, presented as a parody of the GPL v3 license. It mixes a typesetting experiment with a long, story-driven intro on the origin of TeX. Source code and papers are linked from the author's site.
Y65FRxE7uMc.why: HN readers point to it as an example of Tom7's ridiculous-but-brilliant programming projects, here tied to license parody and typesetting.

YAtLTLiqNwg.summary: Sandy Munro interviews Elon Musk at Boca Chica about Tesla production, mega-castings, seats, structural battery packs and the difficulty of mass production.
YAtLTLiqNwg.why: HN uses it as a primary source on Tesla manufacturing and engineering decisions and Musk's grasp of product detail.

YGLNyHd2w10.summary: 2swap explains how he solved the Klotski sliding-block puzzle by mapping its full state space as a graph and visualizing it. The video includes footage of the Guinness world-record solve and links to an interactive graph.
YGLNyHd2w10.why: HN people point to it for intuition about why some games are hard to navigate and for its Rush Hour and graph visualizations.

YMqgiXLjvRs.summary: A fireside chat at LAUNCH Festival 2014 where Paul Graham tells Jason Calacanis why he is handing Y Combinator's presidency to Sam Altman. He also shares startup advice drawn from nine years and 500+ startups.
YMqgiXLjvRs.why: HN people link it for Paul Graham's candid views on startups, Aaron Swartz, and investing selection.

YdOXS_9_P4U.summary: Terence Tao and Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown walk through the cosmic distance ladder, showing how humans measured distances from the Earth to the Moon, Sun, planets and beyond. It includes animations and the history behind each step.
YdOXS_9_P4U.why: HN recommends it as an excellent explanation of how we know cosmic distances.

YdiZa0Y3F3c.summary: Kiran Pamnany's Cambridge Julia Meetup talk on Julia's shared memory parallelism and its new task scheduler. It argues that fork-join and work-stealing models nest poorly and presents depth-first scheduling for composable parallelism.
YdiZa0Y3F3c.why: Recommended in Julia threading threads as an insightful, simple explanation of the new task scheduler.

YNTARSM-Fjc.summary: The first episode of the Yacht Rock web series, a comedic parody about the smooth soft-rock musicians of the late 1970s and early 80s. It is a short, scripted sketch set at Koko's Boat House.
YNTARSM-Fjc.why: HN commenters point the uninitiated to it as a beloved parody series, often in threads that mention yacht rock.

YXylqtEQ0tk.summary: Part 2 of the IROS 2011 keynote by Sebastian Thrun and Chris Urmson on Google's self-driving car. It shows how the car perceives its surroundings with a lidar point cloud and recognizes traffic lights and pedestrians. The audio is poor because it was recorded on a pocket camcorder.
YXylqtEQ0tk.why: HN recommends it as a technical talk aimed at a real engineering audience, with live demos of perception and pre-mapped roads.

YcUycQoz0zg.summary: JPL's David Cummings presents at the 2025 Flight Software Workshop how the team diagnosed and fixed the 2023 Voyager 1 anomaly from billions of miles away. It walks through the flight computer and the memory fix.
YcUycQoz0zg.why: Commenters recommend it for the remarkable remote reverse engineering done on decades-old hardware with no simulator.

Ygty9HxhFK4.summary: An episode of Journey to the Microcosmos, hosted by Hank Green, about diatoms, single-celled algae with glass shells. It covers their role in producing a large share of Earth's oxygen and their uses in beer filtering, paint and kitty litter.
Ygty9HxhFK4.why: HN commenters recommend the series as an excellent, accessible introduction to microscopic life, using this episode as the diatom primer.

Yze1YAz_LYM.summary: Dan Britt lectures on the history of climate, covering orbital cycles, ice ages and conditions millions of years ago. It frames current climate debate with deep-time context.
Yze1YAz_LYM.why: Strongly recommended as a clear explanation of 50-60 million years of climate history that clears up confusion.

YHLU0Uej1WA.summary: A 56-minute fake BBC nuclear attack news broadcast originally made by Ben Marking, re-uploaded in full resolution. It is a fictional breaking-news special depicting nuclear war, and the uploader states it is not real.
YHLU0Uej1WA.why: Commenters bring it up in nuclear-fear and WWIII threads as an unnervingly realistic piece of fictional news coverage.

YJrOuBkYCMQ.summary: Asianometry explains that the worst of the 2021-22 chip shortage sits in trailing-edge semiconductors, not the leading-edge chips usually covered. It covers why those older-node fabs are so hard to expand and fix.
YJrOuBkYCMQ.why: HN commenters point to it as a clear explanation of why fabs aren't being built for older process nodes.

YQ2QtKcK2dA.summary: Yannic Kilcher interviews Emad Mostaque, founder of Stability AI, about the company's funding, its mission, and the release of Stable Diffusion. Topics include access to compute, handling harmful outputs, and avoiding the corrupting influence of profit.
YQ2QtKcK2dA.why: Commenters cite it during Stable Diffusion release debates as a source for Mostaque's vision and Stability's principles.

YUU7_BthBWM.summary: IGN plays through the first episode of the original Doom with its creator John Romero providing commentary. Romero shares stories, design secrets and behind-the-scenes details about the levels, including E1M1.
YUU7_BthBWM.why: HN commenters point to it as a fantastic developer commentary on how Doom's first episode was made.

YdHTlUGN1zw.summary: A 1957 Walt Disney film in which he explains and demonstrates the multiplane camera, the animation tool that gave 2D films depth. It is a short behind-the-scenes piece from Disney's archives.
YdHTlUGN1zw.why: Recommended as a charming primary source on animation technique and for Walt Disney's warm on-camera presence.

YjjTPV2pXY0.summary: A Two Minute Papers episode on NVIDIA's recurrent denoising autoencoder, which cleans up noisy Monte Carlo path-traced image sequences. It shows how a neural network can produce usable renders from very few samples.
YjjTPV2pXY0.why: Cited as an accessible explanation of AI denoising, which underpins real-time ray tracing on RTX hardware.

Yl_K2Ata6XY.summary: Veritasium examines whether food has become less nutritious, weighing soil depletion, selective breeding and rising atmospheric CO2. It evidences nutrient decline even in weeds over a century and ties it to faster plant growth.
Yl_K2Ata6XY.why: HN people recommend it as a short, contextualizing explainer on declining crop nutrient density.

Yo8kfV9kONw.summary: An ABC 20/20 investigation into whether the Better Business Bureau sells its ratings. It looks at BBB finances, executive pay and how grades relate to paid accreditation.
Yo8kfV9kONw.why: HN commenters cite it as evidence that the BBB is a pay-to-play shakedown whenever BBB ratings or accreditation come up.

YsmgPp_nlok.summary: A short clip of George H. W. Bush and Ronald Reagan answering an audience question on illegal immigration at a 1980 Republican primary debate. Both take notably sympathetic positions, including on schooling for undocumented children.
YsmgPp_nlok.why: Repeatedly posted in immigration threads to contrast 1980 Republican rhetoric with modern positions.

YQZ2UeOTO3I.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on how pharmaceutical companies spend billions marketing drugs to doctors. It uses comedy to lay out the industry's questionable practices.
YQZ2UeOTO3I.why: HN uses it as a reference in threads about pharma payments, medical corruption, and declining trust in healthcare.

YXehBx0Yc_w.summary: Corridor Crew dive into the visual effects of Terminator 2 and try recreating the T-1000 bars scene with modern tools. They explain how the original effects were achieved.
YXehBx0Yc_w.why: Recommended in threads about practical versus CGI effects as a fun, instructive attempt to match a classic effect on a small budget.

Y57ruDOwH1g.summary: A long Tsoding Daily programming stream in which he implements hot code reloading in C by loading a dynamic library at runtime without stopping the main program. It also touches on migrating struct versions across reloads.
Y57ruDOwH1g.why: HN commenters cite it as a hands-on example of hot reloading and live coding in C.

YAPt_DcWAvw.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science uses an antique 4x5 view camera to make high-resolution photolithography masks in a home shop. He photographs a poster-sized printout onto litho film to get features around 20 microns.
YAPt_DcWAvw.why: Cited as an accessible way to make lithographic masks at home, in threads about hobbyist chip fabrication.

YAneTFiz5WU.summary: InRangeTV subjects an AR-15 to a mud test in the same mud and location as a preceding AK-47 test. It shows how the rifle runs when covered in mud.
YAneTFiz5WU.why: Cited in AR versus AK reliability debates as evidence that the AR-15 handles mud better than its reputation suggests.

YE8MVNMzpbo.summary: Casey Muratori's remastered BICFest 2018 talk on how the collision system of The Witness was engineered to prevent whole classes of bugs found in game engines. It covers character movement and collision handling.
YE8MVNMzpbo.why: HN points to it as the explanation of how The Witness solved walking and collision.

YGIvWT-NBHk.summary: Alen Ladavac of Croteam talks about continuous integration and automated testing pipelines in games, with case studies from The Talos Principle and Serious Sam.
YGIvWT-NBHk.why: HN points to it as a rare, practical look at how a game studio tests its games and engine.

YJg02ivYzSs.summary: Keiichi Matsuda's short concept film depicting a future where physical and virtual realities have merged and the city is saturated with media and advertising. It shows an augmented-reality-filled daily life as a provocative vision.
YJg02ivYzSs.why: HN cites it as a shorthand for the dystopian risks of ad-driven, ubiquitous AR, usually in critical discussions of advertising and the metaverse.

Y_9vd4HWlVA.summary: Ramesh Raskar presents femto-photography, a technique that captures a trillion frames per second, fast enough to show light itself moving through a scene. He discusses possible uses such as cameras that see around corners or inside the body.
Y_9vd4HWlVA.why: HN points to it as the clearest and most striking explanation of femto-photography, with animations that make it easy to follow whenever related imaging stories appear.

Ya6h2zKlpaQ.summary: An episode of the BSD Now podcast in which Bryan Cantrill joins the hosts to rant about Linux interfaces, alongside the week's BSD headlines. The conversation also touches on containers and related systems topics.
Ya6h2zKlpaQ.why: Cited as a casual, insightful conversation with Cantrill, and referenced for his views on containers and unikernels.

YaUlqXRPMmY.summary: A clip of Richard Feynman contrasting the Greek and Babylonian traditions of mathematical reasoning. It compares the axiomatic approach of mathematicians with how physicists use mathematics.
YaUlqXRPMmY.why: HN cites it when discussing how math should be learned and taught, and why physics isn't built from axioms.

YcVSgYz5SJ8.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews Sarah Paine, a Naval War College historian, about continental versus maritime powers and how that explains decisions by Xi and Putin. They also cover a possible Taiwan war, the fall of the British Empire, WW2 strategy and how to study history.
YcVSgYz5SJ8.why: HN commenters use it as a source for Paine's continental-versus-maritime framework and her views on sanctions when discussing geopolitics.

YdtE3aIUhbU.summary: Arend Schwab demonstrates a research bicycle, the two-mass-skate design, that balances itself without gyroscopic effects or trail. It challenges the common explanations for why a moving bicycle stays upright.
YdtE3aIUhbU.why: HN commenters cite it as the author's own demonstration of research showing that bicycle stability is not explained by gyroscopes.

YeABJbvcJ_k.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment covers the working conditions of US air traffic controllers and the understaffing, outdated equipment (including floppy disks) and funding structure of the FAA. It mixes comedy with policy criticism.
YeABJbvcJ_k.why: HN links it in threads on FAA modernization and controller shortages as an entertaining but substantive summary of the problem.

Ylomy1Aw9Hk.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on how much of a member of Congress's job is now fundraising. John Oliver interviews Congressman Steve Israel about the costs of political spending.
Ylomy1Aw9Hk.why: HN uses it as a go-to overview of the congressional fundraising and lobbying problem whenever money in politics comes up.

YrtANPtnhyg.summary: Pranav Mistry demos SixthSense, a wearable device that projects information onto the physical world and lets people interact with data through gestures. He also shows a paper "laptop" and says he will open-source the software.
YrtANPtnhyg.why: Mostly cited as the origin of ideas later commercialized by products like Humane's projector, and sometimes as a demo that never took off.

YtfzjehDg74.summary: Wildlife videographer Dani Connor Wild talks with Oscar-winning sound designer Mark Mangini about how her red squirrel recording became the desert mouse sound in Dune.
YtfzjehDg74.why: Linked in threads about Dune's sound design as a first-hand interview about the squirrel recording.

YvT_gqs5ETk.summary: A Saturday Night Live sketch for the Amazon Echo Silver, a smart speaker for the elderly, in which older users misunderstand Alexa. It parodies voice assistants.
YvT_gqs5ETk.why: HN brings it up as a joke and as design inspiration for voice assistants for seniors.

Y-Elr5K2Vuo.summary: The classic 1980s anti-drug PSA in which a father confronts his son about drugs and is told 'I learned it by watching you'.
Y-Elr5K2Vuo.why: Quoted jokingly when someone's bad behavior was learned from the very people criticizing it.

Y2F8yisiS6E.summary: Jensen Huang's two-hour NVIDIA GTC March 2024 keynote announcing AI hardware and software advances, including Blackwell, omniverse, robotics and digital twins.
Y2F8yisiS6E.why: Mostly referenced for its specific segments or criticized for misleading performance comparisons, not recommended broadly.

YE9rEQAGpLw.summary: A video showing a virtual camera built in Blender that simulates lenses and film layers using path tracing, to make physically modeled photographs.
YE9rEQAGpLw.why: Cited as an example of simulating the full optical chain of a camera in physically based rendering.

YIWV5fSaUB8.summary: Scam-baiter Jim Browning explains how he fell for a phishing email and ended up deleting his own YouTube channel. He walks through the circumstances and prior incidents that made the scam convincing.
YIWV5fSaUB8.why: Cited as a cautionary example that even security-savvy people can be phished, especially in threads about hacked or terminated channels.

YM5zUwiCTzw.summary: A one-minute clip from Tony Heller's channel in which a Black Lives Matter co-founder describes herself and a colleague as trained Marxists. It is a short political commentary clip.
YM5zUwiCTzw.why: HN commenters mostly cite it as evidence in arguments about BLM's ideology rather than recommending it.

YQIMGV5vtd4.summary: A short demo from the GRASP Lab at the University of Pennsylvania showing a swarm of nano quadrotors flying in coordinated formations. The vehicles were developed by KMel Robotics.
YQIMGV5vtd4.why: HN refers to it as the viral university video that showed what autonomous multicopter swarms can do and helped spark interest in multicopters.

YR5ApYxkU-U.summary: The music video for Pink Floyd's Another Brick in the Wall from the 1982 film The Wall, combining The Happiest Days of Our Lives and Part 2. It includes the schoolchildren and meat grinder imagery.
YR5ApYxkU-U.why: Mostly used as a cultural reference or joke in threads about schools, students and surveillance.

YRyYIIFKsdU.summary: A HOPE XI talk on programming by voice with open source speech recognition. The speaker writes Linux systems code by voice and describes building custom voice grammars as an alternative to the keyboard for programmers with repetitive strain injuries.
YRyYIIFKsdU.why: HN cites it as proof that voice coding works and lists it among resources for programmers who can't type.

YScIPA8RbVE.summary: A London Haskell talk on the algebra of algebraic data types, showing how sum and product types behave like arithmetic. It frames types as numbers obeying algebraic laws.
YScIPA8RbVE.why: Cited as the author's own talk and a way to go deeper on type algebra, with a note that the audio is rough at the start.

YWdD206eSv0.summary: A very short clip from the children's cartoon Arthur riffing on the line about not believing everything you read on the internet.
YWdD206eSv0.why: Used mostly as a joke or cartoon shorthand about misinformation online.

YYLzss58CLs.summary: A short Vox explainer on the duck curve, the shape electricity demand takes in California as solar output grows. It explains why grid operators struggle to balance supply and demand with lots of solar.
YYLzss58CLs.why: Cited as a quick explainer in threads about rooftop solar, renewables, and grid load.

YZFTaEenaHM.summary: A clip from Silicon Valley season 3 episode 2 about Pied Piper's product, satirizing startups and stock-driven companies.
YZFTaEenaHM.why: Mostly posted as a joke or parody reference in threads about SPACs, layoffs and hype.

YZZV464z9g8.summary: Short footage of a Sprint missile from the 1970s Safeguard anti-ballistic missile system launching. The uploader notes the video is not sped up and that this is how fast it takes off.
YZZV464z9g8.why: Linked in missile defense threads as a striking illustration of the Sprint's acceleration and its interception tests.

YbYWhdLO43Q.summary: A viral Squatty Potty ad in which a unicorn demonstrates the supposed benefits of squatting to poop. It is a humorous product pitch about toilet posture.
YbYWhdLO43Q.why: HN mostly shares it as a joke and as an example of surprisingly good marketing.

YcjlhFVTY50.summary: A short clip from the April 1984 Apple IIc rollout presentation at the Moscone Center, uploaded by Alfred DiBlasi. It argues the Apple II line funded the Macintosh's early years.
YcjlhFVTY50.why: HN cites it as period footage showing how Apple presented the II line and how the company leaned on its education market to survive.

Yf1o0TQzry8.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever on time to AGI, what comes after generative models, data limits, alignment, and competing with Google. The title centers on whether next-token prediction could surpass human intelligence.
Yf1o0TQzry8.why: HN commenters cite it mainly for Sutskever's statements that training data is far from exhausted.

YfJ3QxJYsw8.summary: A short clip of Steve Jobs at the D8 conference discussing the post-PC era, including his analogy of PCs as trucks that will remain for a minority of users.
YfJ3QxJYsw8.why: HN uses it as the source for Jobs's truck analogy in debates over whether PCs are dying.

YlGklt4BSQ8.summary: A short Futurama clip lampooning pervasive internet advertising, first aired in March 2000.
YlGklt4BSQ8.why: HN uses it as a joke or reference whenever advertising intrudes into a new medium, since the show predicted it.

YlVDGmjz7eM.summary: A scene from the film Back to School in which Rodney Dangerfield takes his first economics class and brings real-world business experience to a classroom exercise on widgets. It shows the gap between school and the real world.
YlVDGmjz7eM.why: HN commenters bring it up jokingly when a thread involves academic economics versus practical business.

YmcK6GvgVPs.summary: Patreon CEO Jack Conte explains how Patreon thinks about content policy and why it removed the pages of Lauren Southern, members of Defend Europe and IGD. He also describes the company's trust and safety commitments.
YmcK6GvgVPs.why: HN commenters cite it as Patreon's own explanation of the ban, which they find reasonable and sincere.

YpNuh-J5IgE.summary: A one-minute National Geographic clip of researchers Terry Hunt and Carl Lipo testing a theory that Easter Islanders used ropes to rock the moai statues upright to walk them to their platforms.
YpNuh-J5IgE.why: Cited as evidence of how ancient people could move huge stones with only ropes and simple methods.

YtCTzbh4mNQ.summary: A short Reuters news clip showing declassified Russian footage of the 1961 Tsar Bomba, the largest nuclear weapon ever detonated. It shows the blast and the mushroom cloud.
YtCTzbh4mNQ.why: Cited as visual evidence when commenters compare energy scales, such as nuclear yields versus volcanoes or charged bodies.

Yth7O6yeZRE.summary: Full-day livestream of the 2016 Decentralized Web Summit at the Internet Archive, with speakers including Vint Cerf, Tim Berners-Lee, Brewster Kahle, Cory Doctorow and Mitchell Baker. It explores the technology and impact of a decentralized web.
Yth7O6yeZRE.why: Cited as primary footage of web pioneers discussing the future of the internet, such as Berners-Lee's concerns.

YuQqlhqAUuQ.summary: A Futurama clip in which Fry dates a robot, uploaded as a short excerpt.
YuQqlhqAUuQ.why: Cited as a joke or pop-culture reference in threads about AI companions and chatbots.

YwZ0ZUy7P3E.summary: The opening sequence of the film Idiocracy, which satirically shows less intelligent people out-breeding more intelligent ones. It runs about three minutes.
YwZ0ZUy7P3E.why: HN uses it as shorthand in birth-rate and genetics threads, usually half-jokingly and sometimes with pushback that it oversimplifies.
